title: Simit Sesame Ring Bread

seo.imageAlt: Freshly baked authentic Turkish Simit sesame ring bread, golden brown with a crispy sesame crust, ready to eat.
seo.imageCaption: Enjoy the irresistible taste of homemade Turkish Simit, a beloved sesame-crusted bread, perfect with cheese, olives, or jam.

description: Simit is a beloved Turkish ring-shaped bread, generously coated with toasted sesame seeds. Its crispy exterior and soft, chewy interior make it an irresistible street food and breakfast staple. Enjoy this iconic bread with a cup of Turkish tea or cheese and olives.

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the warm water, granulated sugar, and active dry yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until the mixture becomes foamy, indicating the yeast is active.

instructions.title: Prepare and Knead the Dough
instructions.text: Add the flour, salt, and olive oil to the yeast mixture. Mix with a spoon or in a stand mixer with a dough hook until a shaggy dough forms. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until it is smooth, elastic, and no longer sticky.

instructions.title: First Proofing
instructions.text: Lightly oil a clean bowl. Place the kneaded dough in the bowl, turning it once to coat with oil. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let it rise in a warm place for about 1 hour, or until it has doubled in size.

instructions.title: Shape the Simit Rings
instructions.text: Gently punch down the risen dough and divide it into 8 equal pieces. Roll each piece into a long rope, about 18-20 inches (45-50 cm) long. Take one rope and fold it in half, then twist the two halves together to form a spiral. Join the ends to create a ring shape, pressing firmly to seal. Repeat with the remaining dough.

instructions.title: Prepare Molasses Dip and Sesame Coating
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 400F (200C). In a shallow dish, whisk together the 1/2 cup of molasses and 1/2 cup of water. In another shallow dish, spread out the toasted sesame seeds. Dip each shaped Simit ring into the molasses mixture, ensuring it is fully coated, then immediately transfer it to the sesame seeds, pressing gently to adhere a generous layer of seeds on all sides.

instructions.title: Bake the Simit
instructions.text: Place the coated Simit rings on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving some space between them. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until they are golden brown and cooked through. The exact baking time may vary depending on your oven.

instructions.title: Cool and Serve
instructions.text: Once baked, remove the Simit from the oven and transfer them to a wire rack to cool slightly. Simit are best enjoyed warm, ideally fresh from the oven, with Turkish tea, cheese, olives, or jam.

tips: For extra crispy Simit, you can preheat your baking sheet in the oven before placing the Simit on it. This helps create a better crust from the bottom.
If you cant find grape or date molasses (pekmez), you can substitute it with a mixture of honey and a little water, or even pomegranate molasses, though the flavor profile will be slightly different.
Store leftover Simit at room temperature in an airtight container for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze them and reheat in a toaster or oven for a fresh-baked experience.
